plan:
Final experiment design (continuous document, design-only, no execution claimed). The full text was delivered in the assistant turn above containing §1 Rationale, §2 Controls, §3 Analysis plan, §4 Feasibility comprehensive plan covering all ten locked requirements; please refer to that turn as the answer. Summary of the locked choices, all addressed inline:
(i) path A = meta_gradient_ad vs hand-rolled autograd (primary, AD-vs-AD); path B = meta_gradient_ad vs torch.func-only baseline (control isolating torch.func value); path C = implicit_meta_gradient_ad vs unrolled autograd (secondary, separately labelled, never pooled with A/B).
(ii) K grid {5,20,100} for A/B and K up to {100,500} for C.
(iii) float32 main + float64 reference.
(iv) ReLU MLP 128→64→10 (~9,354 params, within the ~10k target) on synthetic in-process 4-class Gaussian-mixture data.
(v) Metrics: perf_counter with 5 warmup steps, wall_first vs wall_steady split; memory as (tracemalloc_peak, rss_delta) pair with CachingAllocator gap documented; numerical stability = float64 FD paired perturbations with both abs-err and rel-err, plus T=50 outer-loss-drift plot with median ± IQR band and per-step paired-Wilcoxon curve under Holm-Bonferroni.
(vi) N=30 paired seeds (20 fallback); Wilcoxon signed-rank, α=0.05; power disclosure honest — design is powered to ~30% effects, not 15%, with optional 5-seed pilot pre-amendment.
(vii) torch.set_num_threads(1) and OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS=1.
(viii) CPU-only; torch.cuda.is_available() checked at startup; no CUDA telemetry used.

Additional requirements (PPTT-1 to PPTT-10) all addressed:
PPTT-1: pin torch==2.1.2 + torchopt==0.9.4 + functorch==0.2.0 + numpy==1.24.4 + scipy==1.10.1 + psutil==5.9.5; smoke-import + dir() logging procedure with three labelled failure modes.
PPTT-2: provenance paragraph + persistent reminder in §1 and footer that API names, signatures and module layout come from public v0.9 README + Feinberg et al. 2022/2023 paper, NOT a local source read; /workspace source absence explicit.
PPTT-3: FD reference — float64, paired perturbations δ = sqrt(eps_fp64)*max(1,|λ|), abs-err = |ĝ − g_FD|, rel-err = |...|/max(|g_FD|,1e-12), reported as median ± IQR + worst-case.
PPTT-4: bit-equivalence audit at K∈{1,2,5} in float64 with max-abs ≤1e-5; abort criterion (failing seeds) recorded; skipped for K>5.
PPTT-5: wall_first reported separately and excluded from wall_steady.
PPTT-6: outer-loss-drift at T=50 with shared seed grid, plot median ± IQR, paired-Wilcoxon per-step with Holm-Bonferroni.
PPTT-7: power justification (σ_log(t)≈0.20 worst-case → 30% effects detectable at N=30); disclosed NOT powered for 15% effects; 5-seed pilot pre-amendment to N=60 if σ_log>0.25.
PPTT-8: threats-to-validity table covering U1–U7 with mitigations.
PPTT-9: full dependency matrix; env-provisioning on CPU box; per-call runtime envelope (~0.2 ms per inner SGD step, ~5 ms per outer step in K=20 baseline, traced first-call ~100–500 ms); total wall-clock budget O(1 hour) on 24-core box with pre-agreed FD restriction (FD only at K∈{5,20} paths A/B; Hutchinson N_hutch=64 path C at K=100 with T=1 reference step; no FD at K=500).
PPTT-10: locked pre-registration block listing software stack, env vars, hardware class, model, synthetic data spec, inner/outer optimizers, T=50, K grid, dtypes, seed list {0…29}, warmup, timing protocol, memory protocol, FD protocol with δ and abs/rel formulas, bit-audit criteria, statistical analysis (paired Wilcoxon + Holm-Bonferroni + Cliff's δ bootstrap CI), power disclosure and pilot-amendment rule.

No fabricated results. The assistant turn above contains the complete document; this handoff metadata confirms stage=result and records that the design-only contract is satisfied.

context.question: Will the explicit gradient differentiation API in TorchOpt, which reuses intermediate data and minimizes memory allocation, reduce computation time and improve numerical stability compared to standard autograd implementations?
context.context: Design an experiment that answers the question. The researcher can clarify source-supported setup details by topic. Do not claim that an experiment was run.
